item.description:
Follow-ups from using 0.5.0's Cursor support in anger. Cursor rows were missing three things the Claude and Codex rows have had all along.
### Added - **Cursor account usage.** A new switch in Settings → Usage shows how much of your Cursor plan's included usage this billing period has spent, as a bar alongside the Claude and Codex ones, with your plan name and when the period resets. You'll also get the same "usage running low" warning the other two give you.
It's **off by default**, and unlike the other two it has to ask Cursor over the internet — Claude and Codex leave their usage figures on your Mac, Cursor doesn't. When you turn it on, Perch reads the login `cursor-agent` already saved and asks Cursor for the number; macOS may ask your permission the first time. Perch only ever reads that login and never changes it. Leave the switch off and nothing is sent anywhere.
### Fixed - **Cursor sessions now show whether they're running in a terminal or in the Cursor app**, with the same CLI badge Claude Code and Codex rows have. Perch had been working this out correctly since 0.5.0 and simply wasn't drawing it. - **Cursor sessions now show which model they're using.** If you're on Auto — the default — the row says "Auto" instead of leaving the space blank, which looked like Perch had failed to detect anything. Pick a model yourself and it shows that name. - **Cursor's logo is now Cursor's actual logo.** The mark shipped in 0.5.0 was drawn from scratch, before the real artwork was to hand, and was the wrong shape — a plain cube, missing the notch that makes it Cursor's.
### Note - Cursor usage is Mac-only for now. The iPhone and watch apps still show Claude and Codex usage only.
